historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (5.3%) sits within 20% of revenue (6.5%) but diverges sharply from EPS (-3.2%), and neither is a clean compounding read: equity CAGR is depressed by $4.2B of buybacks over FY2021-25 (the company distributes most of its FCF), and the EPS CAGRs run peak-to-trough -- FY2022 was the freight-boom peak and FY2025 the fourth year of volume decline. The 3yr revenue CAGR (-4.2%) is the same cycle artefact. Revenue 5yr CAGR (6.5%) is selected as the forward anchor because it spans a full cycle (FY2020 trough to FY2025 trough) and matches the FY2026 run-rate; the base path starts there and decays to 3%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest not stripped, see inputs.interest_income_note). Owner-FCF CAGRs are marginally ABOVE reported because SBC fell from $14.3M to $12.9M -- SBC is not growing faster than cash flow here; the opposite of the DUOL pattern. The real distortion in the FCF series is capex timing: FY2020 (5.6% of revenue) and FY2025 (7.6%) were both low-capex years, so the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR of 6.3% is capex-flattered at both ends and the 3yr figure (1.5%) is cycle-depressed.

scenario_narratives.base: ODFL's two axes are the freight cycle (volume) and yield discipline (price). Base: the cycle bottoms in late 2026 -- Q1 2026 tons/day -7.7% YoY improving sequentially, Q2 +10% revenue on +15% revenue/cwt -- and 2027-28 bring a modest tonnage recovery layered on 4-5% ex-fuel yield, giving 7-8% growth before decay to 3%. Operating leverage on the fixed network lifts the EBITDA margin from 31.4% (FY2025) to a 34.5% plateau, an operating ratio of ~72.5, short of management's sub-70 ambition. The capex pause (FY2026 ~$265M) ends in FY2027-28 as the ~30% excess door capacity is absorbed; capex returns to the 10% of revenue the company has historically spent and settles at 9%. Owner-FCF margin runs ~21% in the trough-capex year, falls to ~17% while capex rebuilds, and matures at ~18%. The stock at ~34x trailing earnings prices a recovery the base case delivers, at a discount rate well below the 9% used here.
scenario_narratives.bull: The industrial economy turns in 2027 and the Yellow-exit share gains repeat: with spare capacity already built and competitors capacity-constrained, ODFL grows revenue 10-11% for two years and sustains high single digits into 2030. Yield stays +4-5% ex-fuel through the upturn. Operating leverage delivers the sub-70 operating ratio management targets (36.5% EBITDA), the level hit in Q2 2026 with property gains. Capex runs heavier to keep 20-25% headroom. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects a structural share gainer in a consolidated industry (top 10 ~82% of LTL).
scenario_narratives.bear: The freight recession becomes structural: tariff-driven manufacturing weakness and nearshoring friction keep LTL tonnage falling through 2028, and the competitive set -- Saia's network build-out, XPO's service push, a standalone FedEx Freight -- turns to price to fill their own new doors. ODFL's premium yield stalls, revenue is flat for two years and the operating ratio drifts back to 75-76 with no leverage. No balance-sheet stress (net cash, no debt), and management keeps investing through the downturn as it always has, so capex never falls below 8.5% -- which is why bear FCF is thin rather than catastrophic. Terminal growth 2.5%, 15x cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis: SBC expensed (trivial here), share count flat, net cash added once, and -- the judgment that matters for ODFL -- capex restored to a mid-cycle 9-10% of revenue rather than the 4.6% trough the company is guiding for FY2026. ODFL is the best operator in a consolidated, rational industry, and the model credits it with a 34.5% mid-cycle EBITDA margin and a decade of above-GDP growth. Even so, at ~34x trailing earnings and ~33x trough-capex FCF, the market is capitalising ODFL at a discount rate several points below the 9% USD WACC used here; the required-return table shows what return the current price implies. The gap between house value and price is a statement about the multiple, not about the business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex normalisation assumption: if ODFL can sustain growth on ~6-7% capex (the FY2020 and FY2026 pattern) rather than the 9-10% modelled, owner FCF is ~$200M/yr higher and the base value rises materially; the 2016-2025 record says it cannot.
Freight-cycle timing: each year the volume recovery slips costs roughly one year of growth at the front of the path, and the market's premium multiple is sensitive to it.

Pricing discipline: LTL yield has risen 4-5% ex-fuel for a decade on industry consolidation; a price war led by newly built competitor capacity would compress the margin plateau toward the bear's 31%.
Discount rate: a long-duration compounder with ~55-60% of value in the terminal; one point of WACC moves the base value by roughly 15-20% (see sensitivity grid).
Operating-ratio ceiling: the bull assumes a sustained sub-70 OR that ODFL has reached only in peak quarters; a structural OR of 72-73 is the base, not a floor.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 126.01-252.03.
data_sources.financials: ODFL_Metrics.csv derived from SEC XBRL companyfacts (10-K FY2025 for FY0 flows, SBC and buybacks; 10-Q Q2 2026 for cash, debt, equity and share count at 2026-06-30). FY2023-25 cash taxes paid from the kpis table. No PDF/text filings exist for this ticker.
data_sources.qualitative: ODFL_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): business model, Q2 2026 results and Q3 2026 guidance (revenue $1.54-1.55B, revenue/cwt +4-4.5%, OR +150-200bps sequentially), FY2026 capex guidance (~$265M), bull/bear points.

inputs.share_count_basis: 208.715M shares outstanding per Q2 2026 10-Q (XBRL, 2026-06-30). ODFL's dilutive securities have run at ~0.1-0.2M shares (<0.1%) in every recent 10-K, so basic and fully diluted coincide to the first decimal; no dilutive-securities table is available on the XBRL path. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks continue (~$120M/quarter), so the count at the valuation date is likely ~207-208M; the filed figure is used with its date.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation, $12.854M). Cash taxes paid on net-share settlement are not carried in the XBRL extract and no filing text exists for this ticker; at 0.23% of revenue the omission is worth well under $1/share.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $730.3M (FY2024 $967.3M, FY2022 $1,277.2M); H1 2026 $239.7M. The flat share count is funded many times over -- ODFL repurchases ~55x its annual SBC. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the cash is counted as SBC and the remainder is a capital-return choice, not value.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.1%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.0 (ODFL five-year beta runs 1.0-1.1) gives a cost of equity of ~9.1%; debt is $20M against a ~$37B market cap, so WACC rounds to 9.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: freight-cycle and pricing risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (owner-fcf-adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. ODFL owns ~95% of its service centers and its fleet; operating lease liabilities are immaterial (well under $100M) and under US GAAP (ASC 842) operating-lease cost already sits inside operating expense, so it is inside the EBITDA margin. Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt and nothing is deducted from the flows -- one treatment, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no minority interests; ODFL is a single-segment, wholly owned operation.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net cash of $264M is ~0.28x the owner-FCF base, below the 1x materiality threshold, and the EBITDA series used for the margin path is operating income + D&A, which excludes interest income. Net cash is therefore added once in the bridge and no interest is stripped from the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2: operating company, cyclical industrial, read with owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fresh build, no prior DCF or memory entry. ODFL is the second-largest US less-than-truckload carrier, a share-gaining compounder whose VOLUMES are cyclical (LTL tons/day down YoY for ~12 quarters through Q2 2026) while yield (revenue per hundredweight +4-5% ex-fuel) has kept margins near record. The cyclical adaptation applied here is to CAPEX, not margins: FY2026 capex is guided to ~$265M (4.6% of revenue) because the network already carries ~30% excess capacity, against a 2016-2025 average of ~11% of revenue. Carrying FY2026's trough capex forward would overstate owner FCF by ~$350M/yr, so the capex path returns to a 9-10.5% mid-cycle level from FY2028 and settles at 9% (D&A ~7% plus ~2% net growth investment, part of it non-depreciating land). FY0 is FY2025 (base_revenue $5,496M, owner FCF $942M); Y1 is FY2026, ~three quarters known (H1 revenue +3.8% YoY, Q3 guided ~+10% to $1.54-1.55B), so Y1 growth of 6.5% is largely locked. The latest fiscal-year TTM (FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025) is revenue $5,602M, EBITDA $1,817M (32.4%, flattered by Q2 2026 property gains), reported FCF $1,115M. Cash tax is modelled on EBIT at 23-25%: FY2023-25 cash taxes ran 22-24% of EBIT because 100% bonus depreciation (made permanent in 2025) defers tax in heavy-capex years; the path starts at 24% in the low-capex FY2026, dips to 23% while capex rebuilds and ramps to the 25% statutory (21% federal + ~4% state) by Y10 per the house ramp-to-normal rule. Working-capital capture is -4% of the revenue change (receivables ~11% of revenue against ~7-8% of operating payables/accruals: growth consumes cash). Horizon is 10 years because the owner-FCF margin is still moving in year 5 as capex normalises. Terminal value is Gordon-bound in base and bull (17.2x and 18.8x FCF against 18x/20x caps); the bear's 15x cap binds against a 15.8x Gordon, worth ~$2/share, deliberately -- a flat-revenue, 31%-margin LTL carrier does not earn a 16x FCF exit.

bear.note: FY2026 is three-quarters locked so Y1 only trims to 6%. From 2027 the freight recession runs a fifth and sixth year, tariff-hit manufacturing volumes keep falling, and well-capitalised rivals (Saia, XPO, FedEx Freight as a standalone, Estes) discount into the gap, so yield growth stalls and the OR slips back to ~75-76 (FY2025 level, no operating leverage). Management keeps investing through the cycle per stated policy, so capex only trims to 8.5-9%.

base.growth_note: Y1 6.5% is the FY2026 run-rate (H1 +3.8%, Q3 guided ~+10%, Q4 ~+8.5%). Y2-Y3 8%/7% assume the freight cycle finally turns in 2027 with tonnage flat-to-up and yield +4-5% ex-fuel, plus continued share gain. Decays to 3% terminal.
base.margin_note: FY2025 EBITDA margin 31.4% (operating ratio 75.2%); H1 2026 33.5% including Q2 property gains. Plateau of 34.5% equals an OR of ~72.5% at 7% D&A -- between FY2025's 75 and management's sub-70 long-term target, roughly the FY2022-24 average OR of 71-72.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided ~$265M (4.6%). Returns to 10-10.5% in FY2028-30 (~$700-790M, the FY2022-24 range) as excess capacity is absorbed, then settles at 9%.

bull.note: Industrial recovery from 2027 drives double-digit revenue growth for two years on the 30% spare capacity already built; operating leverage takes the OR to ~70 (management's target, matched briefly in Q2 2026), i.e. 36.5% EBITDA. Capex runs ~0.5pp heavier than base to keep 20-25% headroom through the upturn.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight down because the bull case needs three independent things to go right -- a volume recovery that has been 'imminent' for three years, yield holding +4-5% through that recovery, and operating leverage reaching an OR of 70 -- and the stock already trades as if the first two are done. Bear weight up because the freight recession is in its fourth year and the competitive set is better capitalised and more aggressive than in any prior cycle (Saia and XPO expansions, FedEx Freight standalone), making a pricing-led downside more plausible than ODFL's history suggests. No going-concern or balance-sheet component in the bear, which is why it does not go higher than 25%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
